newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber higher in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber higher in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices were higher in late trading on Tuesday on the back of rises in Tokyo, but traders said overall market sentiment remained bearish.
"Sentiment remains bearish despite rises in Tokyo because higher offer prices will mean that buyers will turn to other places looking for cheaper rubber," said one trader in Padang, West Sumatra.

"In a way the good sentiment in Tokyo is good for the local market because I believe offer prices would have plunged to 42.00 (U.S. cents/lb) today if prices there did not rise in the last two days," he said.
Tokyo rubber futures ended higher on Tuesday as the weakening of the yen against the dollar stimulated moderate short-covering, traders said.

They said although there were expectations that China may buy some rubber from producing countries, the upside potential in rubber futures would be still limited on rising rubber output in those countries.
Indonesian traders said they also heard China had bought rubber from Singapore.
"I suspect they are buying Thai rubber which is being sold through dealers in Singapore. The prices of Thai rubber is still much cheaper compared with that in Indonesia," said one trader.

"For example, STR20 was done overnight at 41.50, while Indonesian traders were still offering SIR20, whose quality is about the same as the Thai rubber, at 43.00. Buyers are just buying the cheapest rubber available on the market," he said.
Traders said they expected prices to stay unchanged on Wednesday.
"We are hoping that offer prices will be unchanged tommorrow. In general, we expect levels not to quickly drop again like in the past," said one trader.

Traders said deals were done in the afternoon at 43.00 fob Palembang and Padang for September shipment. Offer prices were quoted at 43.50 fob Medan, 43.00 fob Surabaya and 42.75 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
